question: For $x\in[-1,1]$, determine the range of $$f(x)=\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x.$$ Justify whether the function assumes more than one value.
explanation:
Complementary inverse relation
For every $x\in[-1,1]$, the inverse sine and inverse cosine functions satisfy $$\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x=\frac{\pi}{2}.$$

Application to the given function
Substituting this property directly into the definition of $f$, we obtain $$f(x)=\frac{\pi}{2}$$ for every $x\in[-1,1]$.

Range determination
Since the output does not change with $x$, the function assumes only one value. Therefore, its range is the singleton set $$\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}.$$

Endpoint verification
At $x=-1$, $f(-1)=-\frac{\pi}{2}+\pi=\frac{\pi}{2}$. At $x=1$, $f(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}+0=\frac{\pi}{2}$. Thus, even at the endpoints, no additional output value occurs.

options.A: Range: $[0,\pi]$; the function assumes infinitely many values
options.B: Range: $\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$; the function assumes only one value
options.C: Range: $\left\{-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$; the function assumes two values
options.D: Range: $(0,\pi)$; the function assumes every value in this interval
